steps.description: This tour unpacks how `AlchemistV3` tracks **collateral**, **debt** and **earmarking**, how every **user-facing action** mutates that state, and where **access-control** & **invariant checks** gate those flows.
Global state: note cumulativeEarmarked (51), totalDebt (72), totalSyntheticsIssued (75) and the transmuter / adapter / token addresses that external calls rely on.
_accounts (127) holds per-position accounting; _earmarkWeight/_redemptionWeight and _totalLocked (123-119) are the moving global weights applied later by _sync().
Access control modifiers – onlyAdmin, onlyAdminOrGuardian, onlyTransmuter – guard every privileged function.
deposit(): validates args & caps, mints an NFT when needed (365-368), then increments account.collateral/freeCollateral before the ERC20 transfer (376).
withdraw(): ear-marks & syncs first (389-392), checks freeCollateral (393) then decrements balances and transfers yield tokens out (401-402). It finally re-validates collateralization (398-400).
mint(): after access checks it calls _earmark() and _sync(), then delegates real work to _mint(tokenId, amount, recipient).
`_mint()`: uses `_addDebt` (714) to raise per-account & global debt, calls `_validate` (718-720) to enforce collateralization, records `lastMintBlock`, and safe-mints the `ERC20` debt token.
`_addDebt` (852-864) locks collateral proportional to new debt; `_subDebt` (869-885) frees collateral and lowers global totals. Both mutate `totalDebt` and `_totalLocked`.
`burn()`: burns `alAssets` to repay debt; after earmark & sync it computes credit (`464-468`), burns tokens (`472`) and finally calls `_subDebt` (`478`) to update state.
`_earmark()`: once per block queries `Transmuter.queryGraph(...)` to learn how much debt became lockable. It bumps `_earmarkWeight` and `cumulativeEarmarked` accordingly.
`_sync()`: for a given account, applies weight deltas from `_earmarkWeight`/`_redemptionWeight`/`_collateralWeight` to update earmarked, debt, and collateral balances.
`pauseDeposits` and `pauseLoans` – callable by admin or guardian – are the contract’s emergency switches; later `_checkState(!depositsPaused/loansPaused)` enforces them.
`_checkArgument()` helper … and below, `_checkState()` (956-963) – inexpensive invariants used throughout, e.g. `setProtocolFee` (242-247) asserts `fee <= BPS`.

With these pieces in place you can now trace the **full life-cycle**: `deposit` → `mint` (adding debt & locking collateral) → `earmark` (global debt queued for redemption) → `sync` (per-account debt/earmark update) → `redeem`/`burn`/`repay`, all gated by robust access control and invariant checks.
